build: Steam full release 1.x (2023-07-26), store page read 2026-10-15; iOS 4.33.0

package.basis: Desk only, not played: Steam store page and review API (English 397 reviews, 91% positive; 300 sampled), official FAQ, Wikipedia, iOS App Store listing.

fun.source: desk estimate: below Loop Hero (74.0; similar auto-walk hero, stronger feel/aesthetic, but slow opening, waiting-heavy late game and scripting gated at 6-8 h) and at or slightly above Melvor Idle (65.4) for a deeper expert layer; well above the mediocre idle RPG card (30.8)

dims.note: Benchmark Loop Hero matched: one register (animated ASCII for world, UI and portraits), recognisable from one screenshot. No register clash noted in reviews.

dims.note: Rubric ~80 anchor; hand-animated frames praised by independent reviewers. Lapse: some long, unskippable animations (chest opening) read as time-wasting.

evidence.quote: [rec 78690372] The UI is also pointlessly time-wasting and frustrating. The number of clicks you need to do to re-forge

dims.note: Charming and coherent ASCII menus, but crafting/forging is click-heavy and Stonescript relies on external docs.

[rec 151747053] Bosses and areas hold absolute bangers every single time!

evidence.quote: Stonescript is an optional, late-game addition that unlocks when you find the Mind Stone.
The main storyline takes about 6-8 hours.
[rec 117479646] Frustrating at times when I want it to just hurry up

dims.note: Hero walks on his own from minute one and choices are few (loadout, location), so the core act is immediate; but the defining automation layer arrives after the 6-8 h story and the early loop is slow. Rubric anchors it at ~20 on the scripting gate alone; graded 35 because the auto-walk core is clear at once.

evidence.quote: [rec 231020016] a lot of the game is actually about waiting for a long time to get your rewards
[rec 129464427] Gameplay loop is quite simple at the beginning and very slowly things get complex.
It takes a few days to play through all the Legend quests.

dims.note: Story ends at 6-8 h for a casual player, Legend quests run a few days, then an open-ended scripting/farming late game with dailies and time-gated actions. Long walls of waiting are the main complaint.

evidence.quote: [rec 83076293] once you reach the point of being able to automate the farming process with StoneScript, the game changes from frustrating, to enlightening.
an in-game scripting system that allows players to write simple scripts to automate character behavior
[rec 79711301] an actually incredible lack of meaningful content

dims.note: Benchmark (rubric anchor 80): Stonescript is a true expert layer that also mods UI and cosmetics. Lapse: before the Mind Stone the build space is loadout swaps only.

evidence.quote: If you see a red cross † in the location selection screen, that means the game calculates you will die
Un-opened treasures are limited by your character level, up to 400 treasures.

dims.note: PC is one premium price with no IAP. Offline farming exists, bounded by demonstrated performance and a 400-treasure cap, with an honest † death forecast. Lapses: dailies and time-gated actions (rec 231020016); mobile is free-to-play with crystal packs, paid weapons and an 'Advertising' age-rating flag.

dims.note: Loot and boss moments are animated, but reward reveals are slow rather than proportionate; inference from reviews.

dims.note: Short story, then quests, events and an endless scripted farm; longevity is real for scripters, thinner for others.

dims.note: An ASCII auto-RPG you program is visible in one screenshot; nobody else owns it.

evidence.quote: 15 supported languages ... Windows, macOS, and SteamOS + Linux
iOS & Android: On mobile your saved data is stored on iCloud/Google Drive
Languages: English only

dims.note: Five platforms, save export and cloud save on mobile, 15 languages on PC; mobile is English-only and no accessibility settings are documented.

learn.practice: Forecast the absence before it starts: a † on the location screen says the hero would die before collecting everything, and the offline haul is bounded by demonstrated performance, so offline is honest rather than capped by a timer.
learn.evidence: https://stonestoryrpg.com/faq.html a red cross † in the location selection screen, that means the game calculates you will die

learn.practice: An optional expert automation language (Stonescript) gives a ceiling for writers without forcing it on everyone; but it arrives after 6-8 h with little in-game teaching, so a pen should open with worked examples in place.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/appreviews/603390?json=1&filter=all&language=english&num_per_page=100 [rec 158324972] throws a whole scripting language at you once you unlock it, without much of a tutorial

learn.practice: One coherent register for everything (ASCII world, UI and portraits) with hand-animated frames makes a tiny-budget game recognisable and lively.
learn.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_Story_RPG the ASCII art was created frame-by-frame as text and rendered in-engine using custom shaders.

learn.practice: Do not make reward reveals slow; long chest-opening animations read as waiting, not juice.
